title: Carbon Regulation and Competition in the European Airline Industry
abstract: arXiv:2603.27724v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The European Union Emissions Trading System is set to substantially increase the effective carbon price faced by airlines. We estimate a two-stage model of airline competition with endogenous product entry, direct departure frequencies, and pricing. Impacts are highly asymmetric across carrier types and market segments. Consumer surplus declines by up to 34% overall and up to 95% in medium- and long-haul markets. Short-haul markets gain welfare as airlines reallocate capacity toward shorter routes. Airline profits decline by 1--42%, but carbon tax revenue of $1.9--2.9 billion and the social value of avoided emissions of $2.7--4.0 billion more than offset private-surplus losses.

translated_title: 欧洲航空业的碳监管与竞争
translated_abstract: 欧盟碳排放交易体系将大幅提高航空公司所面临的有效碳价格。我们估计了一个包含内生产品进入、直达航班频率和定价的航空公司竞争两阶段模型。研究发现，影响在承运人类型和市场细分之间存在高度不对称性：消费者剩余总体下降高达34%，在中长途市场中甚至下降高达95%；而随着航空公司将运力向短途航线重新分配，短途市场的福利反而有所增加。航空公司利润下降1%至42%，但19亿至29亿美元的碳税收入以及27亿至40亿美元的减排社会价值，足以弥补私人剩余的损失。
tldr: 该研究构建了一个包含内生市场进入、航班频率与定价决策的两阶段航空公司竞争模型，量化评估欧盟碳排放交易体系的影响，发现碳监管的影响在承运人与市场间高度不对称——消费者剩余最多下降34%（中长途市场高达95%）而短途市场福利反而提升，但碳税收入与减排的社会价值足以抵消私人剩余损失。
en_tdlr: Using a two-stage model of airline competition with endogenous entry, departure frequencies, and pricing, this paper quantifies the EU Emissions Trading System's effects, showing highly asymmetric impacts—consumer surplus falls up to 34% (95% in medium/long-haul markets) while short-haul markets gain welfare, and carbon tax revenue plus the social value of avoided emissions more than offset private losses.
